quarterly_data.signal: Q1 (Apr-Jun 2026): revenue JPY 123.2 billion with electronics JPY 75.5 billion; operating profit JPY 26.9 billion with electronics JPY 21.4 billion - driven by strong demand for GPU and high-end CPU, stabilized Cell 8 production and improved utilization at existing plants pushing sales volume above the initial plan, plus strong selling prices for high value-added products. First-half forecast raised: revenue to JPY 253 billion (+10%), operating profit from JPY 38 billion to JPY 54.5 billion (+43%), electronics OP from JPY 33 billion to JPY 47 billion (+44%), net profit from JPY 23 billion to JPY 34 billion (+48%).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue JPY 123.2 billion (electronics JPY 75.5 billion), OP JPY 26.9 billion (electronics JPY 21.4 billion); H1 OP forecast raised 43% to JPY 54.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year FY2026 forecast raised: revenue from JPY 500 billion to JPY 550 billion (+10%), electronics from JPY 350 billion to JPY 375 billion (+14%); operating profit from JPY 90 billion to JPY 127 billion (+41%, operating margin expectation raised from 18% to 23%), electronics OP from JPY 75 billion to JPY 110 billion; net profit raised to JPY 84 billion. Biggest driver: ASP and product mix with a positive impact of JPY 26.5 billion (majority is ASP - the planned quarterly price-reduction curve became less steep or prices were not reduced at all, plus general substrate price increases in an industry-wide supply shortage; not concentrated in a particular customer - GPU, CPU, switching IC and PC ASPs rising across the board). Revenue growth expected in all sub-segments: AI server, switching IC, and general-purpose server/PC.
quarterly_data.figure: FY revenue guide JPY 550 billion (from JPY 500 billion); OP JPY 127 billion (from JPY 90 billion, +41%); ASP/mix impact +JPY 26.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Supply-demand: 'The situation where demand exceeds the industry supply capacity is expected to continue' - substrates are getting larger and more difficult toward next fiscal year and the one after, AI server demand keeps rising, and current selling prices are expected to at least hold at present levels. Customers accepted fewer price cuts, and in some cases none, because of industry-wide shortages. Glass cloth and CCL cost increases are passed through to ASP in a timely manner. Utilization: apart from Intel Cell 5, almost everything was at full capacity utilization; sourcing for the revised FY2026 plan is already secured, though industry-wide competition for materials and equipment could constrain material supply in coming years.
quarterly_data.figure: Demand exceeds industry supply capacity; near-full utilization except Intel Cell 5; prices expected to at least hold

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: Cell 6 and Cell 8 are about 50% through equipment ordering, will commence operations within FY2027 with positive business contribution in FY2028 (timing difficult to accelerate). Next investment decision accelerated - to be made at the latest before the end of the current fiscal year; capacity enhancement is needed across the business ('almost all the customers have asked us to enhance our capacity'), with vacant land at Gama and Ono (would-be Cell 7 and Cell 9) both under consideration at the same time, plus possibly buying another plant building. Advance payments from customers continue to be discussed to fund capacity and offset fixed-cost increases; customer stance on advance payments unchanged from the Cell 6 situation despite an aggressive Taiwanese competitor.
quarterly_data.figure: Cell 6/Cell 8 ~50% of equipment ordered, operations within FY2027, contribution FY2028; new capacity decision before end of FY2026 (Gama and Ono, Cell 7/Cell 9)

quarterly_data.signal: EMIB-T (silicon-bridge embedded substrate): development done by three players including Ibiden, with Ibiden believing it is at the leading edge; a test vehicle has been shipped. Challenges: embedding the silicon bridge in the buildup and getting the interconnection right, plus stronger power supply complicating the core structure (component embedding is a general new trend adding complication) - yield expected lower, but yield has improved a lot since the beginning of development, numbers indicate shippable quality, and there is no showstopper. Small-lot production expected in the latter half of FY2027, mass production at the Gama plant from FY2028.
quarterly_data.figure: EMIB-T small-lot production latter half of FY2027; Gama mass production FY2028; yield improving, no showstopper

quarterly_data.signal: Glass cloth: procurement risks flagged at the beginning of the year have been mitigated. The number of glass cloth suppliers has increased - previously two companies in Japan and Taiwan, now a third and fourth supplier are visible, giving four glass cloth suppliers with visibility for use in mass production; the Japanese glass cloth supplier is increasing capacity, and the tight glass cloth supply situation is expected to simmer down. Ibiden believes it is in an advantageous position in the industry for glass cloth supply. Glass core substrate: joint development continuing (glass core and component-embedding structures pursued as two separate options with their own roadmaps, possibly narrowing to one later).
quarterly_data.figure: Four glass cloth suppliers now visible for mass production (was two); Japanese supplier adding capacity

quarterly_data.signal: ARM-based CPU substrates (AI inference CPU demand): specs will be similar to substrates Ibiden currently supplies and difficulty level similar to the AI GPU work, so Ibiden has the capability to supply. New business is capped at around 20% of the overall in FY2027 - there is no room to allocate more capacity, so large-scale initiatives cannot be undertaken despite expected demand; allocation between new business and value-added products of existing customers to be revisited internally by the mid-year earnings call, when the midterm plan will also be revisited.
quarterly_data.figure: New business capped at ~20% of overall in FY2027 on capacity limits

contracts.signal: Glass core substrate joint development with TSMC confirmed ongoing ('we are doing the joint development effort. We are working with them'): glass core and component-embedding structures are being pursued simultaneously as two separate options, each with its own roadmap; at some point Ibiden may focus on just one of the two, but for now both developmental efforts continue without preassumption.

connects_to.relationship: FCBGA / EMIB-T substrates for Intel packages (dedicated Cell 5 line)

contracts.signal: Intel Cell 5 is Ibiden's one line not yet at full utilization ('apart from Intel Cell 5, almost everything was at full capacity utilization') and its utilization is improving, driving the sales volume increase from existing capacity. For EMIB-T, Core 5 for Intel will be used for small-lot production (targeted latter half of FY2027) before Gama plant mass manufacturing starts in FY2028.
